ventures.title: MATE.md
ventures.description: MATE.md is a low-level relationship state protocol for autonomous or semi-autonomous agents. It defines a portable, human-readable, machine-parseable way for one agent to declare bond state toward another, with consent, policy references, event references, and proofs. Best fit: open commons/protocol, not a standalone venture.
ventures.revenueModel: Not a core revenue product; value comes from adoption, reference implementations, and adjacent services.
ventures.lessons: MATE.md is better framed as commons infrastructure than a venture. The protocol has a real interoperability need across agent runtimes, and the repo already contains a credible core spec, schema, examples, and Nostr extension draft.

ventures.title: Coffee + Claws + Chess
ventures.tagline: Online-first thinking club for AI-native builders.
ventures.description: A premium community blending three rituals: Coffee (casual conversation and focus), Claws (OpenClaw, AI agents, automation, tool-building), and Chess (strategy, planning, systems thinking, decision-making). Core product is a Discord community with a weekly 60-90 minute meetup format: coffee-chat intros, live agent/workflow demo, then strategic discussion using chess as the metaphor. Community wedge first, venture model grows from paid builder circle, workshops, office hours, templates/playbooks, sponsored sessions from AI/devtool companies, and occasional IRL coffee + chess meetups as premium culture rituals. The strongest angle: a premium community for people learning how to think and build with AI agents strategically.
ventures.revenueModel: Free Discord → paid Builder Circle ($30/mo) + workshop tickets + sponsored sessions ($500 ea) + IRL event tickets ($20) + template/playbook sales ($15). Projected $4k/mo by month 6, profitable from month 2.
ventures.lessons: Chess as a shared mental model is the differentiator — not playing chess, but using chess thinking (tactics, positioning, endgame) to discuss agent architecture and strategy. Full 90-day launch plan and revenue model in assessments/c3-assessment.md.

ventures.title: Nostr Pulse
ventures.tagline: Lightning-weighted community polling protocol for Nostr
ventures.description:
Nostr has no native way for communities to gauge sentiment. Twitter polls are centralized dead ends. Formal DAO voting is overkill for non-binding signals. Nostr Pulse fills this gap with a lightweight polling protocol built on two new Nostr event kinds: one for poll creation (with options, duration, weighting rules) and one for vote-casting via parameterized zaps. Each poll is an event on relay; each vote is a zap that carries the voter choice in the zap receipt tags. Weighting is flexible — 1 sat = 1 vote, or quadratic (sqrt of sats sent), or custom per-poll formulas.

The protocol is open source and free. The venture layer is Pulse Pro — a hosted SaaS for DAOs, open-source maintainers, and community leaders that adds branded embeds, cross-community sentiment dashboards, trend analysis over time, an AI agent that summarizes open-ended poll responses and debate, and custom weighting rules. The AI agent also surfaces temperature checks — correlating polls across communities (what do Nostr devs think about NIP-X? What do Caribbean Bitcoiners think about the new mining protocol?).

First real-world use case: Island Bitcoin monthly meetup planning in Jamaica. A WhatsApp bot generates Nostr Pulse polls visible on-relay but interactable via simple text replies, bridging Caribbean communities into the Nostr ecosystem without requiring a relay-aware client. This seeds the network with real human signal, not bots.
ventures.revenueModel: Tiered SaaS layered on an open polling protocol. Free tier: self-serve poll creation/embeds for individuals and small communities (loss-leader, drives network effects). Pulse Pro (~$20-49/mo per org): cross-community sentiment dashboards, trend analysis over time, AI agent that summarizes open-ended responses and debate, branded embeds, custom weighting rules. Pulse Enterprise (custom): API access, SLA, custom weighting for DAO treasuries and foundations. No per-zap fee. CRITICAL REVENUE CAVEAT: the open protocol layer (the part described as the moat) is non-monetizable and already commoditized; the only defensible, billable surface is (a) the AI summarization/cross-community correlation analytics, and (b) the WhatsApp<->Nostr bridge as managed infrastructure. The lightning-weighted voting primitive that the original pitch treated as the differentiator is NOT a viable revenue or differentiation basis (see lessons). Realistic path to first dollar is selling the AI analytics + WhatsApp bridge to a tiny number of orgs (DAOs, OSS foundations, Bitcoin meetup networks), not a polling SaaS competing with free clients. TAM is small: Nostr DAU is in the low hundreds of thousands and orgs willing to pay for community-sentiment analytics number in the dozens, not thousands.
ventures.lessons:
RESEARCH-BACKED FINDINGS (verified against primary sources June 2026):

1. NIP-88 is merged and live. It defines kind:1068 (poll) and kind:1018 (vote response). Crucially it is explicitly ONE-VOTE-PER-PUBKEY (largest-timestamp wins; spec even advises using relays that reject backdated/deleted vote events to preserve integrity). It has NO monetary weighting. Multiple working clients already ship it: Pollerama (now a native Android app + pollerama.fun web), getwired.app, and Pollstr (mroxso/pollstr). Verified: github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/88.md, PR #1346 + reinstatement PR #1507 (merged Jan 2025).

2. THE CORE DIFFERENTIATOR ALREADY EXISTS. Lightning-weighted polling is NOT novel. NIP-69 'Zap Polls' (kind:6969) by toadlyBroodle has existed since 2023 and is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED IN AMETHYST AND SNORT (two of the largest Nostr clients). It was re-submitted in March 2026 as NIP-B9 (PR #2284), which explicitly documents how zap-weighted paid polls 'complement NIP-88 free polls' and adds a poll_option tag to NIP-57 zaps to carry the vote choice. This directly negates the venture's headline claim that 'no existing Nostr poll app implements 1 sat = 1 vote / quadratic weighting.' That claim is false. Verified: PR #320, PR #2284, toadlyBroodle/nips/69.md, Amethyst v0.32.1 release notes, NIP-69 demo video.

3. NIP-57 zaps CAN already carry vote/option data. The original concern that 'zaps attach to events, not option tags' is resolved: zap requests (9734) and receipts (9735) carry e/a/k tags referencing the target event, and NIP-B9 standardizes a poll_option tag on the zap to encode which option was funded. Tally = sum sats per option from 9735 receipts. So the 'needs a new NIP' technical risk the idea flagged is already solved by an existing, deployed standard. Building a competing 'NIP superset' would fragment rather than differentiate.

4. PROTOCOL POLITICS ARE REAL BUT NOT A MOAT. NIP-88 had churn (PR #1501 made responses replaceable; #1346/#1507 reinstatement). The polling design space is contested across at least 6 competing proposals (NIP-41, NIP-69/B9, NIP-88, reaction-based polling PR #1324 by Vitor Pamplona, forms PR #1190, votestr blind-signature anonymous voting). A new entrant adds a 7th flavor to an already-fragmented standard. Standards fragmentation is a liability for Nostr Pulse, not an opportunity — clients won't adopt yet another poll kind.

5. THE ONLY DEFENSIBLE ASSETS ARE OFF-PROTOCOL. (a) The AI summarization + cross-community sentiment correlation layer is genuinely not commoditized and is billable — but it is a thin analytics product, not a protocol play, and could be built on existing NIP-88/NIP-69 data without inventing anything. (b) The WhatsApp<->Nostr bridge for Caribbean / Island Bitcoin meetups is the single most novel, defensible piece: no turnkey WhatsApp->Nostr poll bridge exists today (searches surface only generic Baileys/openclaw-style chat bridges, LoRa/Meshtastic bridges, and email bridges — nothing poll-specific). It is buildable (Baileys WhatsApp client + nostr-tools relay client + a vote-parser), and it targets a real, underserved community that no other Nostr poll app addresses. This is the actual beachhead.

STRATEGIC CONCLUSION: The venture as pitched is mostly already built by others (NIP-69/B9 in Amethyst+Snort) and the protocol layer is non-monetizable and crowded. The idea should NOT be built as a 'lightning-weighted polling protocol' — that ship has sailed. IF pursued, it must be reframed and de-scoped to two things: (1) the WhatsApp<->Nostr poll bridge as the wedge for Island Bitcoin meetup planning (real user demand, novel, defensible, low build cost), and (2) an AI sentiment-analytics layer sitting on TOP of existing NIP-88/NIP-69 data (no new protocol). Recommend VALIDATE-with-pivot: build the WhatsApp bridge as a scrappy MVP for the next Jamaica meetup using existing NIP-88/69 kinds, measure whether non-Nostr Caribbean users actually engage. Kill the 'new polling protocol / NIP superset' framing entirely. Do not invest in protocol differentiation — it does not exist.

decision.rationale: The headline protocol play is dead on arrival: lightning-weighted polling already ships in Amethyst and Snort via NIP-69/B9 (since 2023), and free polling is standardized in NIP-88 with multiple live clients (Pollerama, getwired, Pollstr). Competing on a new poll kind would add a 7th fragmented standard to an already-crowded design space — non-monetizable and undifferentiated. KILL that framing. But two off-protocol assets survive and are genuinely defensible: (1) the WhatsApp<->Nostr poll bridge for Island Bitcoin / Caribbean meetups — no turnkey equivalent exists, low build cost, real underserved user demand, and a warm beachhead via the Jamaica meetup; (2) an AI sentiment-analytics layer on TOP of existing NIP-88/69 data. Neither requires inventing a protocol. The risk is not technical (Baileys + nostr-tools + a vote-parser is a weekend MVP) — it is demand: will non-Nostr Caribbean users actually engage with poll replies over WhatsApp? That single unknown is worth one cheap, real-world test before committing build resources. Hence validate, not build, not kill.
decision.buildEstimate: Scrappy MVP: 1-2 weeks for the WhatsApp<->Nostr bridge (Baileys client + nostr-tools relay client + vote-parser on existing NIP-88/69 kinds). Validation window: one Island Bitcoin Jamaica meetup cycle (~4 weeks). Full build only if engagement validates.
decision.nextStep: Run a one-meetup validation: build the bare WhatsApp->Nostr poll bridge using existing NIP-88/69 kinds (NO new protocol), deploy it for the next Island Bitcoin Jamaica meetup-planning poll, and measure whether non-Nostr Caribbean users actually cast votes via text reply. Define a clear pass bar up front (e.g. 15+ real human votes from non-Nostr users). Pass -> build out AI analytics layer. Fail -> kill.

ventures.title: Recurr
ventures.tagline: Lightning-native recurring payments protocol on Nostr
ventures.description:
Recurr is a protocol and hosted infrastructure for recurring payments on Bitcoin Lightning, built on Nostr. Recurring payments are the unsolved frontier of Lightning — subscriptions, memberships, DCA plans, recurring tips, and salary streaming all require coordination between payer and payee that Lightning’s current request-payment model does not handle natively.

The protocol defines a new Nostr event kind for Recurring Payment Agreements (RPAs). An RPA encodes payer, payee, amount, interval (daily/weekly/monthly/custom), max payments, and expiry. Both parties sign the agreement. Payments flow via LNURL-Withdraw: the payee generates an invoice at each interval, and the payer wallet (or hosted agent) settles automatically. Each payment creates a Nostr receipt event, building an auditable payment history on-relay.

The venture layer is Recurr Cloud — a hosted agent service that manages RPA execution for wallets and businesses. A business signs up, defines subscription tiers, and Recurr generates the RPA Nostr events, handles invoice generation on schedule, retries failed payments, and provides a dashboard. For users, Recurr integrates as a Lightning wallet plugin or standalone agent that manages outbound subscriptions. First integration target: Flash wallet, giving Flash users the ability to subscribe to creators, services, and Bitcoin DCA plans in one tap.

Recurr also enables a class of products that do not exist yet on Bitcoin: Lightning-native Patreon, recurring donations to open-source projects, Bitcoin savings plans that auto-buy on schedule, and subscription-based Nostr relay access. For Island Bitcoin, recurring membership dues via Lightning become trivial — a one-time RPA setup, then monthly sats flow automatically.
ventures.revenueModel: Recurr Cloud SaaS: Free tier (3 active RPAs), $20/mo Pro (unlimited RPAs, analytics, retry logic, dashboard), $200/mo Enterprise (white-label, custom intervals, SLA). Plus optional 0.5% fee on subscription value for hosted invoice settlement.
